articles.headline: Jets rule out RB Hall, WR Mitchell, TE Taylor, LG Parham vs. Bears
articles.description: Running back Breece Hall, wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, tight end Mason Taylor and left guard Dylan Parham were ruled out Friday for the Jets' road game against the Bears.
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- The New York Jets will try to snap a two-game losing streak Sunday without four starters on offense.

Running back Breece Hall, wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, tight end Mason Taylor and left guard Dylan Parham were ruled out Friday for the Jets' road game against the Chicago Bears (2-1). None of them practiced this week.

The offense played well without Mitchell (finger) and Taylor (thumb) last week in their 31-24 loss to the Detroit Lions. Hall (quadriceps) and Parham (knee) were injured in the game, testing the team's depth.

Braelon Allen replaces Hall, who missed only two games in the previous three seasons. Allen, in his third season as Hall's backup, has never rushed more than 12 times in a game in his career.

"It's exciting to know there's going to be a little more on my plate," said Allen, who has 19 carries for 61 yards and one touchdown. "I've been ready for this. This is a good opportunity. I'm super excited for it."

Third-year backup Isaiah Davis, yet to play an offensive snap, is expected to get some work in the backfield as well.

The rushing attack is supposed to be the strength of the offense, but it has generated only 125 yards in the last two games.

"We're not going to get emotionally hijacked by results," offensive coordinator Frank Reich said. "Yes, it matters an incredible amount. Yes, there's an incredible sense of urgency to get results that we and everybody wants, but the best teams and the best players, what we do is we focus on the process, and that's where we get the results."

Jordan Meredith, acquired in a preseason trade with the Las Vegas Raiders, will replace Parham. Meredith, who has 20 career starts, missed a blitz pick-up that resulted in a sack-fumble at the end of last week's game.

Isaiah Williams figures to replace Mitchell again in the starting lineup, with Sterling Shepard again filling the No. 3 role. They plan to elevate Shepard from the practice squad for the second straight week.

Injuries have crushed the Jets at wide receiver. Rookie Omar Cooper Jr., Tim Patrick and Arian Smith are on injured reserve.

There's excellent depth at tight end, so they're positioned to absorb the loss of Taylor. Rookie Kenyon Sadiq figures to have an expanded role for the second straight week. In Detroit, he caught seven passes for 105 yards and a touchdown.

It's a different story on defense. With safety Minkah Fitzpatrick returning from a groin injury that cost two games, the Jets (1-2) are expected to have 10 of 11 starters. The only missing starter is defensive tackle David Onyemata (injured reserve).

articles.headline: Fantasy football last-minute pickups for Week 4: Raymond, Allen, Waller among top options
articles.description: If injuries or tough matchups have you seeking help, Matt Bowen provides options at each key position.
articles.body:
At various points during the fantasy football season, injuries, bye weeks and breaking news can cause you to need reinforcements for your fantasy lineup. Every Friday throughout the 2026 NFL season, Matt Bowen will offer some late-week pickup options at each of the primary fantasy positions to help fill those holes, with an emphasis on deeper leagues.

Because of that, this column will focus mostly on players rostered in fewer than 50% of ESPN leagues, with occasional exceptions.

Looking at the Week 4 NFL slate -- and the available players -- I'll start with the wide receiver position. I have two veteran pass catchers who are seeing consistent volume and producing solid fantasy numbers. There are options at quarterback, too, and one signal-caller could be getting his top target back. We'll also hit on the running backs in line to see an increased role due to injury, plus I have a tight end and a defense to get into lineups.

Wide receivers

Kalif Raymond, Chicago Bears (48.4% rostered; vs. Jets)

The Bears haven't announced whether Case Keenum or Tyson Bagent will start at QB for the Week 4 home game versus the Jets, but either way I'm still pushing for Raymond based on his route deployment in Ben Johnson's offense. Raymond scored 21 points in the Week 3 win over the Eagles, and he has at least five receptions in all three games played this season. Raymond will see the ball as an outlet on crossers, sit routes and unders, plus he has the speed to create big plays (deep over routes and verticals). Raymond fits as a WR3 this week.

Keenan Allen, Indianapolis Colts (46.6% rostered; vs. Commanders)

Allen is a fit for a Colts passing game missing its vertical element with Alec Pierce out with a heel injury. Allen can uncover or make himself available to the quarterback, which we saw in the Week 3 game versus Houston. Allen caught six of a season-high nine targets for 63 yards and a score (18.3 points). Allen has six receptions in two of three games played, and he gets a solid matchup in Week 4 against the Commanders. Managers can start Allen as a WR3.

Dontayvion Wicks (44.7% rostered) and Makai Lemon, Philadelphia Eagles (47.6% rostered; vs. Rams)

DeVonta Smith (hamstring) has been downgraded to doubtful for Sunday's home game versus the Rams, so managers can pivot to Wicks or Lemon, as both should see a bump in target volume. Wicks scored 12 or more points in each of his first two games, with at least four targets in all three this season, while Lemon caught three of four targets for 29 yards in the Week 3 loss to the Bears. I'm really interested in seeing how Lemon performs with an expanded role. The rookie out of USC has the traits to win at the top of the route and he accelerates through the ball.

articles.headline: Former Falcons C, 6-time Pro Bowler Jeff Van Note dies at 80
articles.description: Jeff Van Note, a six-time Pro Bowl center who spent all 18 seasons of his NFL career with the Falcons and was inducted into the team's Ring of Honor in 2006, has died. He was 80.
articles.body:
ATLANTA -- Jeff Van Note, a six-time Pro Bowl center who spent all 18 seasons of his NFL career with the Falcons and was inducted into the team's Ring of Honor in 2006, has died, the team announced Friday. He was 80.

The team did not announce a cause of death.

"We mourn the loss of a true Falcons legend," Falcons owner Arthur Blank said in a statement released by the team. "Jeff Van Note dedicated 18 seasons to this franchise and became one of the most respected and beloved players in our history. He embodied toughness, resilience, humility, and an unwavering commitment to his team, qualities that earned him the admiration of generations of Falcons fans."

Van Note, selected out of Kentucky in the 11th round of the 1969 NFL draft, originally joined the Falcons as a linebacker before being moved to center by then-coach Norm Van Brocklin. He earned the starting job a year later and started 226 of 246 games over his 18-season career. He was a second-team All-Pro in 1979 and 1982.

After retiring in 1986, Van Note became a color commentator and made Atlanta sports radio appearances.

"Jeff's contributions to this organization cannot be measured solely by his accomplishments on the field," Blank said. "He helped shape the identity of the Atlanta Falcons and left a legacy that will endure for years to come. We are grateful for everything he meant to this franchise and our community. On behalf of the Falcons family, we extend our deepest sympathies to his children, Beau, Ben, and Blaine, and all who are grieving this tremendous loss. Jeff will always hold a special place in the history and heart of the Atlanta Falcons."

articles.headline: Erik Ten Hag 'was a piece of c**p' Man United squad - Fred
articles.description: Former Manchester United midfielder Fred has accused ex-boss Erik Ten Hag of being a 'piece of c**p' when it came to squad management.
articles.body:
Former Manchester United midfielder Fred has accused ex-boss Erik Ten Hag of being a 'piece of c**p' when it came to squad management.

The Brazilian spent five years at United, winning the League Cup and reaching the FA Cup final in the 2022-23 season.

Ten Hag came to United with a big reputation, having managed Ajax for four seasons and taking them to the Champions League semifinals but, while he did win the FA Cup and League Cup in his two-and-a-half years in Manchester, things did not quite go as planned with regards to success in the Premier League.

And Fred, who left the club to join Turkish side Fenerbahce during Ten Hag's tenure ahead of the 2023-24 season, gave a damning review of his time under the Dutchman.

"Ten Hag was tactically very good, but with the group he was a piece of c**p," he said on the Charla Podcast.

"He argued with everyone. He argued with me, with Cristiano [Ronaldo], with Casemiro, with Rashford... He wouldn't put me in to play, sometimes it got stressful.

"[With Ten Hag] Only his Dutch players played. A clique-ridden coach. But, tactically, one of the best I've ever worked with.

- Sir Alex Ferguson on David Beckham's Preston loan: 'He thought I wanted him gone but that's not true'

- Sir Alex Ferguson was 'terrified' about Old Trafford return after brain surgery

- Rasmus Højlund hits 'Siuuu' against Portugal: 'Cristiano Ronaldo will never be forgotten'

"He wanted the team to run, but Cristiano [was already] older. He took Cristiano out (of the starting lineup), and then there was a falling out."

Ronaldo left the club at the end of the 2022 season after he found himself no longer in the starting lineup.

Ten Hag was sacked in October 2024, with United 14th after seven matches -- their worst start since the 1989-90 season.

Fred also lifted the lid on other United managers he experienced, including Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, the 1999 treble winner who took the helm at the club in December 2018 after Jose Mourinho was sacked.

The 33-year-old, who has 32 Brazil caps, gave his assessment of both of those managers, who he had much more positive things to say about.

"Solskjaer was good with the group, but he was helped [in training] by the assistants. He united the group," Fred added.

"Mourinho's a great bloke, he is funny. I've just been with him at Fenerbahçe; he brought me to United.

"Before Ancelotti came along, his name was being mentioned for the national team [Brazil].

"So I'd show him the rumours and he'd say: 'F*** off, mate. I'm not going anywhere. I'm going to manage my club here.' A really decent bloke."

articles.headline: Raphinha set to be fit for Barcelona clashes with PSG and Real Madrid - source
articles.description: Raphinha will be fit for Barcelona's double header against Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid later this month after tests revealed no major injury to his right thigh on Friday, a source told ESPN.
articles.body:
Raphinha will be fit for Barcelona's double header against Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid later this month after tests revealed no major injury to his right thigh on Friday, a source told ESPN.

Raphinha, 29, was taken off at half time of Brazil's 4-2 win over Australia on Tuesday after feeling some discomfort in his thigh.

He was subsequently removed from the Brazil squad for Saturday's game against India and flew back to Barcelona, were he underwent tests on Friday.

A club source told ESPN those tests had confirmed Brazil's initial assessment, that Raphinha "has edema in the thigh rather than an injury."

The news comes as a major relief to Barça after alarm bells were set ringing on Tuesday when Raphinha was taken off.

The forward missed 25 games for club and country last season due to a hamstring problem in the same thigh and there were fears he had suffered a relapse.

Despite the good news, sources say Barça will manage the player's minutes with caution ahead of some massive games in October.

Barça, who have won all eight of their matches this season, return to action after the international break on Oct. 10 against Getafe.

- UEFA receives Real Madrid dossier on Barcelona-Negreira case

- Clásico match ball for Barcelona vs. Real Madrid LaLiga clashes unveiled

- Transfer rumors, news: Several Premier League clubs eye Koundé move

In theory, Raphinha could feature in that game, but coach Hansi Flick will make a decision on his participation in the days before the fixture.

Barça then travel to Galatasaray and Real Betis before a huge week which sees them face PSG in the Champions League on Oct. 20 and Madrid in LaLiga on Oct. 25.

Raphinha has been a revelation for Barça so far this season, shining in a new role as the team's No.9 after the exits of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres.

He has netted 14 times in eight appearances, including back-to-back hat tricks in his last two club games.

articles.headline: Former Man City manager Roberto Mancini 'not concerned' about charges
articles.description: Former Manchester City manager and current Italy coach Roberto Mancini says he is unconcerned about being implicated in the financial rule-breaking scandal engulfing the English club, which on Friday said it was appealing the verdict.
articles.body:
ROME -- Former Manchester City manager and current Italy coach Roberto Mancini says he is unconcerned about being implicated in the financial rule-breaking scandal engulfing the English club, which on Friday said it was appealing the verdict.

In his latest comments on the issue, Mancini said: "It's not a problem that concerns me" -- despite appearing to acknowledge last weekend before a Nations League match in Turkey that he had "a double contract" as City coach from 2009-13.

Among the raft of charges that City has faced is an alleged failure to provide accurate details for player and manager payments between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

In 2018, German magazine Der Spiegel published evidence showing Mancini doubled his base salary of 1.45 million pounds (now $1.9 million) for advising a club in Abu Dhabi.

City has been accused of potentially avoiding paying about 12 million pounds ($16 million) in income tax and national insurance in relation to Mancini's salary, The Telegraph reported this week.

Mancini was asked if he was worried about the case ahead of Italy's match in France on Friday.

"No. I already spoke it about the other night. It's not something that concerns me. It's City's problem, unfortunately," Mancini said late Thursday at the Stade de France.

"It's not a problem that concerns me," Mancini added, repeating himself. "Look, really. I already said it the other day in Turkey."

- How Man City players, staff are handling Premier League verdict

- Man City appeal guilty verdict in Premier League breaches case

- Manchester City guilty charges explained: Premier League's options, how appeal works, more

In Turkey, Mancini said that "Manchester City is not guilty and the fact of having a double contract isn't my problem but theirs, probably."

Mancini led City to its first titles after Abu Dhabi's ruling family had bought the club in 2008, winning the FA Cup in 2011 and in 2011-12 coaching the team to its first Premier League title in a half century.

He was fired days after a shocking loss to Wigan in the FA Cup final in 2013.

City has protested its innocence throughout the long-running case, which reached a milestone Tuesday when the Premier League published a verdict saying the club was "guilty of all charges related to serious breaches" of the competition's financial rules from 2009-18.
